transcript.content: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in. I, uh, I hope I'm not wasting your time with this. I'm sure a lot of it is probably just a normal part of getting older and adjusting, right? 

But, well, what brings me in is that since I stopped working, I just... I can’t seem to slow down. I try to be good and take it easy like everyone tells me to, but I'm just up and moving from one little job around the house to the next, all day long. It’s almost like I still have a crew waiting on me to get things moving, if that makes sense? I just can't seem to turn it off and sit in my chair. Is that an okay reason to come see you?

{"intent": "Determine whether the patient's restlessness is a lifelong trait from childhood or a recent change.", "question": "Looking back, is this feeling of needing to be constantly on the go something

Well, you know, I guess if I really think about it... it's kind of always been there? I hope that doesn't sound too strange. Even way back when I was a kid in grade school, I remember my teachers telling my parents that I was a bright boy, but just a little... scattered, I suppose you could say. 

I was always misplacing my pencils, or I'd get too excited and just blurt out the answers before raising my hand. They always had to remind me to actually finish my assignments before I ran off for recess. But, you know, boys will be boys, right? I just had a lot of energy. Does that sound like the kind of thing you're asking about, Doctor?
When you feel like you can't slow down, is that driven by worry or anxiety about things going wrong?

Oh, no, no, I wouldn't say I'm worried about things going wrong. I hope I didn't give you the impression that I'm an anxious person! I really try to just take things as they come, you know? 

It's more just... well, it's just this physical feeling, like a motor running inside me that I can't quite switch off. It's not that I'm fretting over the bills or worrying about the roof leaking or anything like that. It's just that if I sit down, my foot starts tapping, or I feel like I need to get up and check on the tomatoes, or organize the garage. It's just energy, really. Not worry. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it right.
